shots.phrase: Begin by framing Pipeline Foundations as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Consider this worked case: A learner maps the inputs, constraints, and observable result for Pipeline Foundations, then checks each step against the stated claim.
Arrow connects each box sequentially.
Now define Image Representation precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: A 100x100 pixel grayscale image becomes a 10000-element array where each value ranges from 0 to 255.
Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them.
With the foundation in place, examine how Color Conversion operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: Converting an RGB image to HSV separates color information from brightness, allowing algorithms to isolate specific hues regardless of lighting intensity.
Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition.
Next, compare the choices involved in Filtering and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: A Gaussian blur filter averages adjacent pixel values to reduce sensor noise and highlight large-scale object boundaries.
Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts.
Apply Feature Methods to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Consider this worked case: SIFT (Scale-Invariant Feature Transform) identifies keypoints and generates descriptors that remain consistent across scale and rotation changes.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Calibration, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: Using a chessboard pattern, the system calculates focal length and principal point to map 2D image coordinates to 3D space accurately.
State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable.
Stress-test the reasoning around Geometric Transforms with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Consider this worked case: Affine transformation adjusts image coordinates to correct perspective distortion in a tilted photograph.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Segmentation to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Consider this worked case: Thresholding separates foreground objects from the background by classifying pixels based on intensity values above or below a set level.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Motion Methods to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Consider this worked case: Optical flow calculates pixel displacement between consecutive frames to track object movement and estimate velocity.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Evaluation & Robustness as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
Consider this worked case: Varying the threshold value changes the number of detected edges, demonstrating how sensitivity to illumination and noise affects detection accuracy.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
